title: PCPO: Proportionate Credit Policy Optimization for Preference Alignment of Image Generation Models
claim: Under identical prompts and seeds, baseline policy-gradient outputs collapse into blurry, homogeneous or artifact-ridden images, while ours stays diverse and high-fidelity.
layout: 2 panels stacked, each a baseline-over-ours image grid, row labels at left
description: A two-part qualitative image grid. Panel (a) is a 2x6 grid of small images: the top row, labeled DDPO, shows animals and flowers (cat, bear, butterfly, rooster, flower, camel) in a similar soft, blurry painterly style. The bottom row, labeled Ours, shows the same subjects, but with sharper detail, more varied colors and compositions, and a bee in place of the flower. Panel (b) is a 2x3 grid of large images. The top row, labeled DanceGRPO, shows a winged demon amid ornate decoration, a monkey with sunglasses and headphones, and a matador with a bull and a bowl of noodles. These are dark and cluttered, with visible artifacts. The bottom row, labeled Ours, shows the same prompts rendered brighter, cleaner and more coherent. Row labels are rotated at the left edge, and (a) and (b) captions sit below each panel. The eye goes first to the vivid, saturated images.
caption: Qualitative comparison of baseline methods (top) and PCPO (bottom) on identical prompts and seeds. PCPO mitigates model collapse seen in baselines across different frameworks. (a) DDPO (SD1.5, Aesthetics): At a matched reward level, PCPO preserves diversity and fidelity while DDPO collapses into a blurry, homogenous style. (b) DanceGRPO (FLUX, HPSv2.1): After training for 200 epochs, PCPO achieves both a higher reward and superior image quality, avoiding artifacts observed in the baseline.
abstract: While reinforcement learning has advanced the alignment of text-to-image (T2I) models, state-of-the-art policy gradient methods are still hampered by training instability and high variance, hindering convergence speed and compromising image quality. Our analysis identifies a key cause of this instability: disproportionate credit assignment, in which the mathematical structure of the generative sampler produces volatile and non-proportional feedback across timesteps. To address this, we introduce Proportionate Credit Policy Optimization (PCPO), a framework that enforces proportional credit assignment through a stable objective reformulation and a principled reweighting of timesteps. This correction stabilizes the training process, leading to significantly accelerated convergence and superior image quality. The improvement in quality is a direct result of mitigating model collapse, a common failure mode in recursive training. PCPO substantially outperforms existing policy gradient baselines on all fronts, including the state-of-the-art DanceGRPO. Code is available at https://github.com/jaylee2000/pcpo/.
